subject: Post-call recap: Acme long-context eval - recommended models & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: Acme long-context eval - recommended models & next steps

Hi Sarah - great to meet today, and thanks for walking us through the PDF export and how you rely on 200-300k token conversation histories for your legal summarization flows. Quick recap and proposed next steps below.

Summary of needs:
- Primary goal: high-fidelity summarization of multi-document case files (~150-300k tokens) with minimal hallucination and strong attribution.
- Constraints: on-prem deployment for PII (will be via Redwood Private), 99th-percentile latency SLO of ~6s for interactive recaps, and deterministic truncation behavior for auditability.
- Evaluation interest: compare model candidates on summarization fidelity, reference retention, and truncation degradation over long contexts.

Recommended immediate next steps (proposed):
1) Run a focused long-context eval using a 3-part prompt set (attached: acme_prompt_set_v1.csv) that includes: full-context summarization, incremental update summarization (streaming additions), and targeted Q&A with document references.
2) Benchmark models we recommend for this workload (attached sheet: redwood_model_recs.xlsx):
   - rwd-instruct-70b-ctx256k (quantized) - best balance of fidelity and cost for very long contexts; recommended for canary.
   - rwd-llama3-34b-ctx128k - lower cost option; watch for citation fidelity on merged docs.
   - open-70b-32k - strong on short-context precision; expected to degrade with truncation beyond 32k.
3) Run our automated truncation/regression harness (we'll provide a Drive folder link) with three dataset slices: 1) <32k, 2) 32-128k, 3) 128-300k to surface where summarization fidelity drops.
4) Plan a 2-week canary on a subset of production traffic (10k sessions) with automatic fallback to smaller-context model for latency spikes.

Attachments: acme_prompt_set_v1.csv, acme_long_context_benchmarks.pdf, redwood_model_recs.xlsx

I'll schedule a short kickoff next Wed to hand off eval access and share the Drive folder. Do you want us to provision an on-prem evaluator VM, or would you prefer to run the harness and we consume results?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142
From: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Wright <ben.wright@acme.com>, Acme Data Team <data@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Acme long-context eval - recommended models & next steps

Thanks Marissa - this is super helpful. A couple quick answers/questions:

- We can run the harness internally; prefer that for security. Please send the evaluator checklist and a lightweight VM image or container spec so our infra team can mirror.
- Important: we need deterministic truncation behavior documented. If a model drops earlier context, we need explicit indicators in the output (e.g., "...context trimmed at 128k tokens"). Can Redwood provide logging hooks or tokens to mark truncation?
- Budget: initial evaluation budget is ~ $30k USD. If the canary looks good we can discuss dedicated capacity.

Also, Ben asked whether Redwood has prior benchmark PDFs comparing summarization fidelity across context lengths - the deck you mentioned. Could you send the benchmark PDF and any shortnotes on evaluation metrics you use?

Cheers,
Sarah
Head of Data Products | Acme Corp
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Acme long-context eval - recommended models & next steps

Hi Sarah - thanks for the quick reply. Answers inline and next artifacts attached.

- Evaluator run: we'll share the harness container spec and a minimal runner script (you'll find it in the Drive folder link). It runs locally and emits a CSV of per-example metrics (ROUGE-L, citation-precision, hallucination-flag, truncation-point).
- Truncation indicators: yes - our runtime emits a structured header when context is trimmed and writes a truncation marker to the token stream. For Redwood Private/on-prem we can enable an additional log line (X-REDWOOD-TRUNCATED: true, TRUNCATED_AT_TOKENS=128000) to appear in traces. That should satisfy auditability/forensics.
- Benchmarks: attached acme_long_context_benchmarks.pdf and a shortnotes doc in Drive that explains our scoring (we prioritize citation-precision and human-rated factuality for these tasks).

Recommended model plan (concise):
- Canary: rwd-instruct-70b-ctx256k (quantized) - expected best fidelity at 128-256k windows, but costs ~2.2x per-token of the 34b.
- Fallback: rwd-llama3-34b-ctx128k - keep as automated fallback for latency spikes / cost control.
- Long-term: evaluate cross-checking pipeline - summarize with the 70b model, then run a lightweight citation verifier (34b) for extracted references to reduce hallucinations.

Next steps:
1) I'll upload the harness and a short runbook to the Drive folder tonight.
2) Can we lock the kickoff for Wed 11/10 11:00 PT? I'll invite infra + legal for a 30-min sync.
3) Please share an access email for your infra run and the preferred VM spec (CPU/RAM/disk) so we can pre-seed data.

HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deal/ACME-4521
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmeBenchmarks

Best,
Marissa
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap: Acme long-context eval - recommended models & next steps

Looping you both on the final confirm from Sarah. For the kickoff we should prepare:
- Container image + quickstart script (we'll pin to v1.0)
- Truncation log header enabled by default for Private evals
- Cost estimate for 2-week canary (10k sessions) across the two model variants; include GPU-hours and expected quantized throughput.

Markus - can you take ownership of the cost spreadsheet and draft a short runbook for the infra handoff? I'll draft the legal/access checklist.

Thanks,
David
